scheme_name: National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm: Custom Hiring Centre cum Harvester Groups
description:
The National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India in 2016. 

This mission aims to reduce the country's dependence on imported edible oils. 

India is one of the largest consumers of edible oils globally. 

The country imports about 60 percent of its edible oil requirements. 

The mission specifically focuses on increasing domestic production of oil palm. 

Oil palm is a high-yielding crop that can significantly enhance oil production. 

The initiative aims to promote the cultivation of oil palm in suitable regions across India. 

The primary objective of the mission is to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production. 

The government has set a target to increase oil palm cultivation to 1 million hectares by 2025-2026. 

The mission also aims to increase the production of crude palm oil to 10 million tonnes by 2025-2026. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm includes the establishment of Custom Hiring Centres. 

These centres are designed to provide farmers with access to modern agricultural machinery. 

The Custom Hiring Centres aim to reduce the cost of cultivation for oil palm farmers. 

The government provides financial assistance for setting up these centres. 

The assistance can go up to 50 percent of the total cost incurred in establishing the centre. 

The maximum financial assistance for setting up a Custom Hiring Centre is capped at ₹50 lakh. 

The Harvester Groups are another essential component of this mission. 

These groups consist of farmers who come together to share resources and knowledge. 

The Harvester Groups facilitate collective farming and resource sharing. 

This approach helps in reducing individual costs and increasing efficiency. 

The government provides training and capacity-building programs for these groups. 

The training covers best practices in oil palm cultivation and management. 

The mission also emphasizes the importance of research and development. 

The government collaborates with various agricultural universities and research institutions. 

This collaboration aims to develop high-yielding and disease-resistant oil palm varieties. 

The mission has a specific focus on promoting oil palm cultivation in the northeastern states of India. 

These states have suitable climatic conditions for oil palm cultivation. 

The government aims to encourage farmers in these regions to adopt oil palm farming. 

The mission also includes financial support for farmers. 

Farmers are eligible for a subsidy of up to ₹30,000 per hectare for oil palm cultivation. 

This subsidy is provided for the first five years of cultivation. 

The government also supports the establishment of nurseries for oil palm seedlings. 

The nurseries are crucial for providing quality seedlings to farmers. 

The mission has set a target to establish 50 nurseries across the country. 

Each nursery is expected to produce around 1 lakh seedlings annually. 

Farmers interested in oil palm cultivation must meet specific eligibility criteria. 

They must have a minimum landholding of 2 hectares for oil palm cultivation. 

Farmers should also be willing to form or join a Harvester Group. 

The application process for the Custom Hiring Centres involves several steps. 

Farmers must submit an application to the Department of Agriculture in their respective states. 

The application should include details of the proposed centre and estimated costs. 

Farmers must also provide a project report outlining the objectives and benefits. 

Required documents include land ownership proof and identity verification. 

Once the application is submitted, it undergoes scrutiny by the department. 

Upon approval, the financial assistance is disbursed in installments. 

The first installment is released upon the establishment of the centre. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The mission has a timeline for implementation and monitoring. 

The government conducts regular reviews to assess the progress of the mission. 

The reviews help in identifying challenges and making necessary adjustments. 

The implementing authority for this mission is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Oil Palm Mission is coordinated by the National Mission on Edible Oils. 

Farmers can contact the local agricultural department for more information. 

The government also conducts awareness programs to educate farmers about the mission. 

These programs aim to inform farmers about the benefits of oil palm cultivation. 

The mission has received positive feedback from farmers in pilot regions. 

Farmers have reported increased income and reduced dependence on imports. 

The initiative aligns with the government's broader goal of achieving Atmanirbhar Bharat. 

Atmanirbhar Bharat translates to self-reliant India. 

The mission also contributes to rural employment generation. 

It creates job opportunities in cultivation, processing, and marketing of oil palm. 

The government aims to create a sustainable oil palm industry in India. 

This industry has the potential to boost the rural economy significantly. 

The mission is expected to enhance the livelihoods of thousands of farmers. 

The government continues to promote oil palm as a viable alternative crop. 

The initiative is part of a larger strategy to enhance agricultural productivity. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm is a crucial step towards food security. 

It addresses the challenges of rising edible oil prices in the country. 

The mission is a comprehensive approach to achieving self-sufficiency in edible oils. 

Farmers are encouraged to participate actively in this mission. 

The government is committed to providing the necessary support and resources. 

The success of the mission will depend on the collective efforts of all stakeholders. 

This includes farmers, government agencies, and research institutions. 

The National Mission on Edible Oil- Oil Palm aims to transform the edible oil landscape in India. 

It is a forward-looking initiative that seeks to empower farmers and boost production. 

The mission holds the promise of a sustainable and prosperous future for oil palm cultivation in India.
